howto.name: Add your ODT files
howto.text: Drop or select one or more OpenDocument Text (.odt) files, up to 25 at a time and up to 500 MB each. Templates (.ott) and flat .fodt files are turned away as an unsupported file type, so save them as .odt first; for Word files, use Office to PDF.

howto.name: Convert with LibreOffice
howto.text: Click ODT to PDF. There are no settings: each file is uploaded and converted on the server by LibreOffice in headless mode, one file at a time, with a fresh LibreOffice profile for every conversion.

howto.name: Know the default PDF settings
howto.text: PrivaTools passes no export options, so LibreOffice's standard PDF export settings apply. Headings become bookmarks and comments in the document are left out. Photos may be recompressed as JPEG at quality 90, and images sharper than 300 DPI are scaled down to 300 DPI. The result is not PDF/A.

howto.name: Download the PDF
howto.text: Each file becomes its own PDF named after it, so minutes.odt downloads as minutes.pdf. A single file downloads automatically; several can be saved one by one or together as odt-to-pdf-results.zip.

faq.q: Will the PDF look exactly like the document in LibreOffice?
faq.a: Close, but not always exact. The server's LibreOffice is installed without extra font packages, so text in a font the server does not have is set in a substitute, which can move line and page breaks. Blank pages that LibreOffice inserts automatically, for example so a chapter starts on a right-hand page, are left out. Check the page count before you send the PDF.

faq.q: What does a typical conversion look like?
faq.a: A thesis.odt with numbered headings, photos and review comments becomes thesis.pdf with a bookmark for each heading and no comments. Five sets of meeting minutes queued together come back as five PDFs, which you can download one by one or as one ZIP.

faq.q: Are formulas made in LibreOffice Math converted?
faq.a: Yes. When LibreOffice saves an .odt, it stores a drawing of each formula, and the PDF shows that drawing, so a formula looks as it did when the file was last saved, except that a font the server does not have is replaced, as in the rest of the document. In a file without those drawings, which some other programs write, the server's LibreOffice Math module lays each formula out again in the server's fonts, so it can look slightly different from your screen.

faq.q: Do macros run during the conversion?
faq.a: No. LibreOffice opens a file for conversion without permission to run macros, and PrivaTools passes no setting that changes this, so nothing a macro would add or change on opening appears in the PDF.

No. Comments in the document are left out of the PDF. PrivaTools passes no export options, so LibreOffice's default export settings decide, and those leave comments out; the page has no setting to include them.

faq.q: Can I convert a password-protected ODT?
faq.a: No. No password is passed to LibreOffice, so it cannot open the file, no PDF is produced and the page reports "Processing failed. Please try again." Save a copy without the password in LibreOffice and convert that.

faq.q: How large a document can I convert, and how long can it take?
faq.a: Up to 500 MB per file. Each conversion has two minutes; one that runs longer is stopped and the page reports "The server took too long. Try a smaller file or try again." The converter also accepts up to five files a minute from one IP address, so in a longer queue some files can fail with a rate-limit message; wait a minute and click Retry.

faq.q: What happens to my document after I upload it?
faq.a: It is uploaded over HTTPS and converted on the PrivaTools server in isolated temporary per-request storage, by LibreOffice running there rather than a third-party service. LibreOffice works on a temporary copy with its own temporary profile, both cleared when the conversion ends. Response cleanup removes the upload and the PDF after your download is sent, and a background sweep clears anything an interrupted request leaves behind. Nothing is added to an account or file library.
